description: Khronos glTF-Sample-Assets 'CesiumMan' -> werk canonical humanoid v1. A COLLADA2GLTF export with 19 joints and no naming convention at all, which is why it is in this test set: the names carry no information a heuristic could use, the left and right sides are named differently from each other, and the rig has no clavicles, no spine2 and no separate head bone.
derivation: Assigned by reading the rig's own geometry, not by name similarity. Each joint's role was fixed by where its HEAD sits and how long the segment to its child is: Skeleton_arm_joint_L__4_ has its head 9.1 cm lateral of the chest and a 24.2 cm segment to its child, so it is the upper arm and not a clavicle; Skeleton_arm_joint_L__2_ is a leaf at the end of an 18.5 cm forearm, so it is the hand. The right side's chain is 14 -> 15 -> 16 named 'R', 'R__2_', 'R__3_' while the left side's is 17 -> 18 -> 19 named 'L__4_', 'L__3_', 'L__2_' -- the numbering runs the other way, and mirroring the left map by string substitution would silently swap the shoulder and the wrist.
unmapped_canonical_note: This rig has no clavicles and only three torso joints. Nothing is invented to fill them: the canonical clavicles and spine2 hold their rest rotation relative to their nearest mapped ancestor, and the arms hang off spine3 exactly as they do on the source.
